case_study_insert.main_stem: Axiom Security Software (AXS) is a private limited company in the cybersecurity software and digital services sector, employing a workforce of 50. Founded in 2013 by Noah Bergman, the business operates a flat structure with laissez-faire leadership. AXS plans to invest $880,000 in an automated penetration-testing platform with a self-service client portal, financed by a $580,000 five-year bank loan and $300,000 retained profit. It has fixed costs of $400,000 a year, a variable cost of $14 a unit and a selling price of $46, and currently produces 35,000 units a year. AXS faces a people and quality problem: staff turnover has reached 14% and the defect rate in software patches has risen, causing complaints about missed deadlines.
case_study_insert.appendix_1_marketing_ops: Quality and HR Report — Q3 2025: AXS released 2,100 software patches, with a defect rate of 4.1%, up from 2.2% a year ago. Complaints about missed deadlines rose from 22 to 41 per month, and average patch turnaround is 3.8 days. Staff turnover reached 14%. A survey of 380 clients found 66% value automated security testing and 53% would pay $5 more per month for faster patching.

appendix_2_financial_data.title: Extract from the Statement of Profit or Loss and Capital employed data of Axiom Security Software for the year ended 31 March 2025 ($ '000)

case_study_insert.appendix_3_external_environment: Economic and Business Bulletin (November 2026): (1) The central bank has raised the base interest rate from 3.9% to 4.7%. (2) The national minimum wage will rise by 5.6% from $15.20 to $16.05 per hour from January 2027. (3) Specialist developer software licences and cloud testing costs have risen 8.9% year-on-year, and cybersecurity spending grew 9.4% in the same period.

questions.question_text: AXS is financing part of its testing-platform expansion with a five-year bank loan. Explain two advantages for AXS of using retained profit to fund the expansion instead of the bank loan.
questions.model_answer:
Point 1: Retained profit needs no interest payments or fixed repayments, so AXS keeps the cash that would otherwise service the $580,000 five-year bank loan. That cash can cover fixed costs of $400,000 a year and the work on the $880,000 penetration-testing platform while turnover is 14%, without adding to the pressure that has already produced 41 monthly complaints.

Point 2: Using $300,000 retained profit keeps control with Noah Bergman's team rather than a lender, so no external conditions dictate how the self-service client portal is developed. It also avoids pledging assets when the 4.1% defect rate and 14% staff turnover still need attention, giving the 50-strong firm room to stabilise quality before taking on more debt. The 53% who would pay $5 more for faster patching shows where internally saved cash can be reinvested, rather than paying interest that would compete with the $400,000 fixed costs and the 14% turnover problem.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for each valid advantage identified (max 2).
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for detailed contextual explanation and analysis applied to AXS and its financing decision.

questions.question_text: AXS is launching its automated penetration-testing platform. Consider a cybersecurity conference sponsorship, search-engine advertising, or social media influencer marketing. Which should AXS choose to promote the launch? Justify your recommendation.
questions.model_answer:
Cybersecurity conference sponsorship: A conference stand lets AXS demonstrate the platform to specialist buyers and builds credibility in a technical market. However, stand and travel costs are high for a 50-employee firm already servicing a $580,000 loan, and only a small delegate audience sees the product, too narrow to support 35,000 units of volume.

Search-engine advertising: Ads shown to people searching for penetration testing reach high-intent buyers and can be controlled by budget. The weakness is that text ads cannot demonstrate the platform, and cost per click can rise quickly; with a $880,000 investment to justify, AXS needs to show the product, not just describe it.

Social media influencer marketing: Security reviewers can demonstrate the platform and the self-service portal to a large professional audience at low cost per view, with measurable engagement. This suits the 66% of surveyed clients who value automated security testing and the 53% who would pay $5 more for faster patching, and it lets AXS address the 4.1% defect-rate issue by showing how the new platform finds faults earlier.

Recommendation: AXS should choose social media influencer marketing. It demonstrates the product, reaches technical buyers cheaply and scales beyond one conference. Conference sponsorship is rejected as costly and narrow; search advertising is rejected as unable to demonstrate a visual platform. Influencer content should be supported by targeted search ads for high-intent buyers. With the 4.1% defect rate and 41 monthly complaints, AXS should promote a solution it can demonstrate; a static conference stand or text advert cannot show the platform reducing faults, whereas a reviewer can.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Limited outline of the promotional options with minimal application to AXS.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Detailed discussion of at least two options in the context of AXS with some judgement.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Detailed discussion of all three options with a well-justified recommendation explaining why conferences and search ads are rejected.

questions.question_text: AXS has 14% staff turnover and a rising defect rate. Explain two benefits for AXS of using laissez-faire leadership within its flat structure to motivate its software developers.
questions.model_answer:
Point 1: Laissez-faire leadership gives experienced developers freedom to choose how they fix the 4.1% defect rate in the 2,100 patches, which can raise ownership and job satisfaction. Autonomy suits skilled security specialists and may reduce the 14% turnover, because developers who control their own methods are more likely to stay and take pride in reducing the 41 monthly complaints.

Point 2: The flat structure lets developers act on ideas without seeking several layers of approval, helping shorten the 3.8-day patch turnaround and speeding work on the $880,000 testing platform. With fewer managers, decisions about client priorities reach the 50 staff quickly, supporting Noah Bergman's aim of recovering from the rise from 2.2% to 4.1% defects. Autonomy is most valuable when the 50 developers are skilled, which is why it can reduce the 14% turnover; however the 4.1% defect rate still needs a shared standard, so leaders should set minimum quality expectations even in a flat structure.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for each valid benefit identified (max 2).
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for detailed contextual development linked to AXS's turnover, defect rate and patch turnaround.

questions.question_text: AXS wants to reduce its 14% staff turnover. Consider a performance-related bonus or job enrichment through team working. Which should AXS choose? Justify your decision.
questions.model_answer:
Performance-related bonus: Linking pay to patch quality or speed can motivate the 50 developers to cut the 4.1% defect rate and shorten the 3.8-day turnaround. It is simple to understand, but it costs money that AXS must find while servicing a $580,000 loan and funding an $880,000 platform, and it does not change the repetitive work that may be driving the 14% turnover or the 41 monthly complaints.

Job enrichment through team working: Giving developers varied tasks and shared responsibility for the self-service portal makes the work more interesting and uses their security skills fully. This can reduce turnover by addressing the cause rather than paying around it, and team review of patches can catch faults that produced the rise from 2.2% to 4.1%. The drawback is that it takes time to organise and relies on the flat structure functioning well.

Decision: AXS should choose job enrichment through team working. It tackles the 14% turnover at its source, can improve the 4.1% defect rate and costs little compared with a bonus. The performance bonus is rejected as an expensive short-term fix that does not relieve the repetitive patching behind the 41 complaints, though a small bonus could be added later once the platform is running smoothly. AXS can measure the choice against the 14% turnover, the 4.1% defect rate and the 3.8-day turnaround, all given in the insert. Since no bonus cost is stated, the comparison is qualitative: team working addresses the cause of turnover while a bonus only rewards output after the fact. The flat structure already supports team working, so the change needs little new spending at a time when $580,000 of loan repayments and an $880,000 platform must be funded.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Basic description of a bonus and job enrichment with limited application to AXS.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Detailed analysis of the benefits and drawbacks of both options in the context of AXS.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Comprehensive evaluation of both options with a well-justified decision covering turnover, cost, quality and motivation.

questions.question_text: Calculate and explain how AXS's management can use its cost, break-even and productivity data.

sub_parts.model_answer: Formula: Break-even output = Fixed costs ÷ Contribution per unit. Substitution: $400,000 ÷ ($46 − $14) = $400,000 ÷ $32 = 12,500 units. Answer: break-even output is 12,500 units a year.
Formula: Contribution per unit = Selling price − Variable cost per unit. Substitution: $46 − $14 = $32. Answer: contribution per unit is $32.

sub_parts.question_text: Explain four ways AXS's management can use this financial data.
sub_parts.model_answer:
1. Compare the 12,500-unit break-even output with 35,000 patches produced, giving a margin of safety of 22,500 units, so managers can see how far demand can fall before the $880,000 platform stops covering costs.
2. Use the $32 contribution per unit to test pricing: a $4 cut to $42 leaves $28 contribution, so about 14,286 patches (400,000 ÷ 28) would be needed to cover the $400,000 fixed costs.
3. Average total cost is about $25.43 a unit ($400,000 ÷ 35,000 = $11.43 plus $14), below the $46 price, leaving scope to absorb higher licence costs.
4. Labour productivity is 700 patches per worker (35,000 ÷ 50), a benchmark for checking whether team working and the new platform lift output despite the 4.1% defect rate.

questions.model_answer: (i) Break-even output = 12,500 units | (ii) Contribution per unit = $32 | (iii) Four contextual uses: margin of safety of 22,500 patches; a $4 price cut leaving $28 contribution and about 14,286 patches needed; average total cost of $25.43 against $46; labour productivity of 700 patches per worker.

working_marks: 1 mark for correct formula/method and 1 mark for the accurate numerical answer in (i) and (ii); 1 mark for each valid applied use in (iii).

questions.question_text: Using Appendix 2, evaluate AXS's financial position by calculating the gross profit margin and the profit margin for 2024 and 2025. Has AXS's financial position improved? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer:
Calculations:
Gross Profit Margin 2024 = 45.0%
Gross Profit Margin 2025 = 50.0%
Profit Margin 2024 = 20.0%
Profit Margin 2025 = 25.0%
ROCE 2024 = 14.0%
ROCE 2025 = 17.5%

Detailed workings: 2024 revenue 980, cost of sales 539, gross profit 441; operating profit 196; capital employed 1,400. 2025 revenue 1,176, cost of sales 588, gross profit 588; operating profit 294; capital employed 1,680. Gross profit ÷ revenue: 441 ÷ 980 and 588 ÷ 1,176. Operating profit ÷ revenue: 196 ÷ 980 and 294 ÷ 1,176. Operating profit ÷ capital employed: 196 ÷ 1,400 and 294 ÷ 1,680.

Evaluation: Every measure is better in 2025. The share of revenue left after direct costs rose from 45.0% to 50.0% because revenue grew by 196 while cost of sales grew by only 49, so the software service is becoming more efficient. The share retained as operating profit also rose, and the return on the 1,680 of capital employed improved, which matters because AXS must service a $580,000 loan while investing $880,000 in the testing platform. The 14% turnover and 4.1% defect rate remain risks, but they have not prevented stronger profitability.

Conclusion: AXS's financial position has improved. Both margins and the return on capital are higher, with revenue growing much faster than cost of sales. Management should use the stronger margins to fund job enrichment and quality improvements so that turnover and defects do not reverse the gain. Interest payable of 36 in 2025 is modest beside operating profit of 294, so financing costs are not undermining the improvement.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: States financial figures or changes without accurate ratio calculations.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Accurately calculates the two margins for both years with contextual analysis of the trend.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Accurate calculations for both years, detailed evaluation of revenue, cost, profit and capital trends, and a justified conclusion on whether AXS improved.

questions.question_text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage for AXS of introducing a self-service client portal for its security-testing service.
questions.model_answer:
Advantage: The survey of 380 clients found 66% value automated security testing and 53% would pay $5 more per month for faster patching, so a self-service portal can convert that demand into extra revenue and reduce the 41 monthly complaints about missed deadlines. The additional contribution helps cover $400,000 of fixed costs and supports the $880,000 platform.

Disadvantage: Building and maintaining the portal adds to the $400,000 fixed costs or the $14 variable cost per unit, and with a 4.1% defect rate already present a buggy portal could create more complaints rather than fewer. The insert gives no portal cost, so its exact return cannot be calculated from the data provided. The portal should be tested against the 4.1% defect rate before launch, because a faulty self-service system would add to the 41 complaints rather than reduce them. The 66% who value automated testing support the idea, but delivery must match the claim.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for a valid advantage and 1 mark for a valid disadvantage.
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for detailed contextual development linked to AXS's survey, defect rate and costs.

questions.question_text: Using Appendix 3, evaluate how the base interest rate rise to 4.7%, the 5.6% minimum wage increase to $16.05 and the 8.9% rise in specialist software licence and cloud testing costs will affect AXS. Which change will have the greatest impact? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer:
Interest rate rise (3.9% to 4.7%): If the $580,000 five-year bank loan is variable-rate, the extra annual interest is 0.8% × $580,000 = $4,640 a year, shown as 0.008 × $580,000. This is modest against $400,000 of fixed costs, and if the loan is fixed the direct cost is zero. Higher rates may still slow the 9.4% growth in cybersecurity spending.

Minimum wage increase (5.6% to $16.05 an hour): The insert gives no hours worked or current pay, so an annual wage cost cannot be invented. The derived measure is productivity: 35,000 patches ÷ 50 workers = 700 patches per worker. If that holds, the wage rise can be absorbed; if the 4.1% defect rate and 14% turnover reduce output, unit labour costs rise and the $32 contribution falls. The direction is clear but the size cannot be quantified here.

Input-cost inflation (8.9%): The $14 variable cost is not split into components, so an explicit upper bound is 8.9% × $14 = $1.246, about $1.25 per patch. Across 35,000 patches that is 35,000 × $1.25 = $43,750 a year. Even a smaller rise reduces contribution from $32 toward about $30.75 and increases the number of patches needed to cover $400,000 of fixed costs above 12,500.

Conclusion: The 8.9% rise in software licence and cloud testing costs will have the greatest impact. It applies to every one of the 35,000 patches and directly erodes the $32 contribution that must cover $400,000 fixed costs and service the $580,000 loan, whereas the interest rise is about $4,640 and the wage effect is unquantifiable and partly offset by productivity. AXS can recover part of the increase through the $5 faster-patching premium that 53% of clients accept.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Identifies the external factors with limited application to AXS.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Analyses the impact of at least two external changes on AXS's costs, revenue or financing in context.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Detailed evaluation of all three changes with shown derivations from insert figures and a well-justified greatest-impact judgement.
